title: Apply Fails: Resource Already Exists
intro: You wrote Terraform for the company's existing 'assets-prod' S3 bucket so it can finally be managed as code. The apply fails immediately.

steps.prompt: Run the apply to see the exact error.
steps.fake_output:
aws_s3_bucket.assets: Creating...
Error: creating S3 Bucket (assets-prod): BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou: Your previous request to create the named bucket succeeded and you already own it.
steps.hint: Terraform tried to CREATE something that already exists.

steps.prompt: Terraform doesn't know the bucket exists because it isn't in state. Confirm that.
Bring the existing bucket under Terraform's management instead of creating a new one.
steps.fake_output:
aws_s3_bucket.assets: Importing from ID "assets-prod"...
Import successful!
steps.hint: import records an existing resource in state at the address you wrote in code.

steps.prompt: Check whether your code matches the real bucket's configuration.
steps.hint: After an import, plan shows every difference between your code and reality.

resolution: Terraform only manages what's in its state. A resource created by hand (or by a different Terraform project) is invisible to it, so writing a resource block for it makes Terraform try to create a duplicate. 'terraform import' fixes that by recording the existing resource at your code's address. The follow-up plan matters just as much: it revealed the code would change versioning to 'Suspended' — but the real bucket has versioning ENABLED, and suspending it would stop protecting objects from accidental overwrites. Adjust the code to match reality first, get a clean plan, and only then start making deliberate changes. On Terraform 1.5+, an 'import {}' block does the same thing reviewably in a pull request.
